title: Regional failover + backpressure metrics and circuit-breaker dashboards
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective: Instrument a cohesive set of metrics and dashboard panels to make multi-region failover behavior, service-level objectives, and backpressure/circuit-breaker state visible end-to-end. This ticket covers SLI definitions, PromQL/metrics naming, alerting thresholds, Grafana dashboard layout, and a small agent-side telemetry patch to capture tokenized-response timers and queue-depth histograms.

Background: We have intermittent latency escalations during regional failovers and spikes where autoscaler cold starts + request surges cause queueing and degraded p95/p99 for customer-facing routes. Existing dashboards surface high-level token latency but do not show queue growth, inflight shards, or circuit-breaker trip counts by region. Engineers struggle to reason about whether degradation is due to routing, kernel contention, or downstream storage timeouts.

Goals:
- Define SLIs that reflect end-to-end and per-token progress: time-to-first-token, per-token-generation-ms histogram, and tail token latency for p99.9.
- Create golden-signal panels focused on failover: regional error rate, regional success rate, request reroutes, and cross-region retry counts.
- Add backpressure instrumentation: request_queue_depth, worker_backpressure_count, and circuit_breaker_open{region,route}.
- Write PromQL queries and example thresholds for alerts and SLO burn-rate compute.
- Ship a compact telemetry change on the serving agent to emit queue_depth histogram and token_time_ms summary (small patch, runtime-1.22).

Acceptance criteria:
- New Grafana dashboard with sections: Overview (SLO health), Region Health, Backpressure/Queueing, Circuit-breaker Activity, Token-level latency heatmaps.
- Prometheus metrics exposed with agreed naming and labels, documented in the metrics registry.
- Three new alert rules: SLO burn > 3x for 5m, queue_depth > 200 for 2m, circuit_breaker_open_rate > 5/min.
- Runbook updated with guidance for failover investigation steps and mitigation (reroute rules, emergency throttle settings).

Telemetry / metric names (proposed):
- redwood_request_count_total{region,route,status}  # counter
- redwood_request_reroute_total{from_region,to_region,route} # counter
- redwood_token_time_ms_bucket{le,region,route}  # histogram buckets per token generation
- redwood_time_to_first_token_ms_summary{region,route}  # summary for TTF token
- redwood_request_queue_depth{region,pool}  # gauge (atomically sampled)
- redwood_worker_backpressure_count{region,pool}  # counter incremented when worker signals backpressure
- redwood_circuit_breaker_state{region,route,state}  # gauge {open=1,closed=0,half_open=0.5}

PromQL examples (to be copied into alerts):
- Token p99 example: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(redwood_token_time_ms_bucket[5m])) by (le, region, route))
- Queue pressure: avg_over_time(redwood_request_queue_depth{pool="inference"}[2m]) > 50
- Circuit-breaker open rate: increase(redwood_circuit_breaker_state{state="open"}[5m]) > 3

Runbook excerpt (short):
1) Check dashboard Overview -> See if SLO burn is localized to single region or global.
2) Inspect Region Health -> Look at redwood_request_reroute_total to see if requests were rerouted.
3) If queue_depth elevated: scale capacity or enable emergency shedding (see page: confluence.redwood.com/Playbooks/Backpressure).
4) If circuit_breaker tripped: refer to mitigation steps (manual reset allowed for non-critical customers).

Notes on implementation approach:
- Instrumentation: add two small counters/histograms in serving runtime (kernel scheduler path) to avoid expensive allocations; emit via existing prometheus client. Patch limited to ~40 lines.
- Dashboard: new folder under Grafana: "Reliability / Multi-Region Failover" with exported JSON. Layout set for 4 rows; each panel includes region filter and route variable.
- Alerting: wire alerts into PagerDuty for P0 routes and Slack channel #reliability for P1.

Links to artifacts: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-runtime/pull/2293, Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/RELIABILITY/Multi-Region+Failover+Metrics, Draft dashboard JSON: https://grafana.redwood.com/dashboards/rel-mrf-2026/draft

Dependencies / follow-ups: need coordination with networking team for accurate from_region label (ENG-7988), and QA to validate metric cardinality (ENG-8017).
